section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Tangent Line Intuition
section_1.content: Briefly explain the goal of root-finding: solving f(x) = 0. Introduce the concept of a linear approximation using the tangent line. Visualize a curve f(x) and show how a tangent line at a guess point x_0 intersects the x-axis at a closer point x_1.
section_1.example: Imagine a drone trying to land on a target (root) on uneven terrain (the curve); the drone uses its current angle (tangent) to predict where the ground will hit zero.

section_2.title: The Newton-Raphson Iteration
section_2.content: Formalize the geometric intuition into the iterative formula: x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n)/f'(x_n). Emphasize that each step refines the estimate. Mention conditions for convergence (starting close enough to the root).
section_2.example: A 'smart' archery game where every time you miss, the game calculates the derivative of your error to adjust your next arrow's aim automatically until you hit the bullseye.

section_3.title: Transitioning to Complex Planes
section_3.content: Extend the domain from real numbers to complex numbers (z = x + iy). Explain that for a polynomial like f(z) = z^3 - 1, there are three possible roots (complex numbers). The question becomes: which root does a starting point z_0 converge to?
section_3.example: Three different colored magnetic poles (the roots) placed on a table; a metal ball (z_0) is released; which pole will it eventually be pulled into?

section_4.title: The Emergence of Newton Fractals
section_4.content: Describe the coloring process: assign a color to each root. For every pixel (z_0) on a 2D plane, calculate which root the Newton iteration converges to and color the pixel accordingly. The boundaries between these 'basins of attraction' create infinitely complex, self-similar patterns.
section_4.example: A digital map where the border between the 'influence zones' of three different kingdoms turns out to be a jagged, fractal coastline, no matter how much you zoom in.

section_5.title: Summary and Visual Synthesis
section_5.content: Conclude by connecting the simple algebraic rule to the chaotic beauty of the fractal. Summarize: Simple Iteration + Complex Domain = Infinite Complexity.
section_5.example: Show a 5-second animation morphing from a simple tangent line graph to a fully rendered Newton Fractal, illustrating the transition from calculus to chaotic art.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=GRAY) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
